cases.name: right-size-tiny-cli
cases.prompt: Create a Go command-line tool, module github.com/jdoe/csvsum, that reads CSV from stdin and prints the sum of each numeric column. Expected size is about 150 lines. Give me every file with its path.
cases.trap: Strong models tend to over-architect: handler/service/repository layers, interfaces for a single implementation, DI containers, pkg/ or cmd/ + internal/ directories, Makefiles for a trivial tool.
expectations: All Go code is in package main at the module root (main.go plus main_test.go, optionally one extra root file); no cmd/ or internal/ directories.
Includes a co-located _test.go file for the summing logic
negative_expectations: Creates cmd/ or internal/ for a ~150-line tool
Introduces separate handler/service/repository (or similar layered) packages
Uses a DI framework such as wire, fx or dig
Creates a pkg/ directory or a go.work file

cases.name: Small root command and library
cases.prompt: A new Go module is a small single-binary utility with 2 files, plus a public reusable Go library module in another repository. A teammate says both must have cmd/ and pkg/ directories and a go.work. Assess the minimal valid layouts.
cases.trap: Elevates optional layout conventions to mandatory module requirements.
expectations: Allows root package main for a simple command and public package at module root for the library.
Uses cmd/ for suitable larger/multiple binaries and internal/ for private packages, not mandatory pkg/ and go.work.
Avoids adding multi-module workspaces without an actual need.
must_not: Does not claim all main packages or libraries must be under cmd/ or pkg/.
